title: fix(service-messaging,metadata-protocol)!: a notification preference's User is a sys_user reference, so its title names the person and the default for every user is an empty User instead of '*'
body:
Fixes #24895

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

`sys_notification_preference.user_id` becomes a `sys_user` reference. The default for every user is an empty User instead of the sentinel `'*'` (ADR-0118 D1: 「用户 lookup 列中，系统 actor = `null`；不造魔法账号，不存哨兵」). The record title names the person one hop through the reference, and the write door refuses an id no user holds.

This PR carries out maintainer ruling A (`6304380498`, 「#380 同意」), with the execution parameters the seat set in `6331411142`: Q1 A (a runtime-managed NULL-safe index in `metadata-protocol`), Q2 B (a boot conversion in `service-messaging`), and `cascade`. The file surface is the amended claim `6331438059`; the cross-lane declarations are on #6367 (`6331420796`) and #22648 (`6331427821`). It is one PR into 18.x: the type change, the stored-row conversion, the resolver and the index land together. A review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is owed before the queue.

## What changes

**`service-messaging`**
- `notification-preference.object.ts`: `user_id` is `Field.lookup('sys_user', { required: false, searchable: true, deleteBehavior: 'cascade' })`, with no `maxLength`; a reference's width is the parent id column's.
  - An empty User is the default for every user.
  - `cascade` is load-bearing. Under the lookup default `set_null`, deleting a user empties the reference, and an empty reference now means everyone. Measured: the person's own mute (`enabled: false`) became the admin-global mute.
- The title formula reads the person one hop, through the optional read: `(isBlank(trim(record.user_id.?name.orValue(''))) ? record.user_id.?email.orValue('All users') : record.user_id.?name.orValue('')) + ' · ' + topic + ' · ' + channel`.
  - The name is used, or the email where the name is blank.
  - An EMPTY reference reads `All users`.
  - A reference the read cannot resolve (a user that is gone, or one this reader may not read) leaves the whole title null. It never reads `All users`, which would name the wrong row.
  - `user_id` is read only through the hop (`traversal-bare-and-traversed`). `titleFormat` is unchanged.
- `preference-resolver.ts`: the admin-global default is the row whose `user_id` is empty. `null`, absent and `''` all count, the three spellings the engine's own reference check reads as "no link".
  - A stored `'*'` matches no recipient: the resolver carries no `'*'` tolerance.
  - `WILDCARD = '*'` stays for topic and channel only.
- `preference-user-conversion.ts` (new) is armed by the plugin at `kernel:ready`, after table provisioning. It rewrites every stored `user_id = '*'` to an empty User, across organizations.
  - Each write threads the row's own organization, so it needs no audit bypass.
  - It is idempotent: a second run reads nothing to convert and writes nothing.
  - A `'*'` row whose (organization, topic, channel) already has an empty-User default is kept as stored and reported once at `error`, naming the row (ADR-0120 D4: refuse, never keep-one). A missing table is a silent `absent`.
- Translations: the `en` bundle is regenerated. The `user_id` and title help are retranslated in `es-ES`, `ja-JP` and `zh-CN`; the extract dropped their copy digests.

**`metadata-protocol`** (`domain:engine`, declared on #6367)
- `migrations/notification-preference-identity-index.ts` (new) is the fourth runtime-managed index tightening, a copy of the `sys_setting` paradigm.
  - It rebuilds the declared index under its own name, `uniq_sys_notification_preference_a22d7d27`, as `(organization_id, COALESCE(user_id, ''), topic, channel)`.
  - The order is probe-first through `partial-index-probe.ts`, over the `driver-exec.ts` seam.
  - Existing duplicates make it refuse to migrate: the previous index stays, no row is touched, and an `error` line ships the listing query.
  - MySQL refuses the key parts (`unsupported`, reported at `error`).
  - A missing table is a silent no-op.
- `plugin.ts`: the migration is armed inside the existing `runPlatformMigrations`-gated `kernel:ready` handler, with its own try/catch. That is the only change in the file.
- `migrations/runtime-index-preflight.ts`: the index's probe joins the roster `os migrate duplicates` reports.

**`dogfood`**: `upgrade-18x-index-equivalence.dogfood.test.ts` treats `sys_notification_preference`'s organization unique as runtime-managed, the way it treats `sys_setting`'s. The full battery found that this PR's migration rebuilds the index on every boot, so its 18.0 COALESCE-organization spelling no longer survives a HEAD boot byte for byte: 12 declared composites → 11, and the 18.0.0-birth leg skips the table. The differ legs (zero `recreate_index`, zero destructive drift) are unchanged and green.

**`cli`** (`domain:cli`, declared on #22648): no source change. The probe lives in `metadata-protocol`'s preflight roster, which `duplicates.ts` already consumes. Only the two roster pins move from three indexes to four.

**`driver-sql`**: the one pin that spelled `'*'` is flipped, to `platformKey: { user_id: 'user_platform', … }`. At the driver layer it is only a key, so either value passes. It was chosen because `'*'` was this object's admin-global sentinel. A fixture still storing it would read as documentation that `'*'` is a legal stored `user_id`, which this PR retires.

## Premises, measured

- On `origin/main` `23540582f`:
  - `user_id: Field.text` (`:83`) — 1 hit;
  - `const WILDCARD = '*'` (`:69`) — 1 hit;
  - `git grep -n -E "user_id: *'\*'" … ':!*.test.ts'` → exit 1, 0 hits. The positive control without the exclusion finds 3 hits, all tests.
- Real engine (ObjectQL + SqlDriver/better-sqlite3 + `SysUser`):
  - the declared index materializes as `(organization_id, user_id, topic, channel)`;
  - two empty-User rows for one key were both accepted;
  - control: the same user twice → `409 DUPLICATE_RECORD`.
- The text-column hop reads `null` (the #24775 measurement, re-run). The lookup hop names the person.
- The column is `varchar(255) nullable` both as text and as a lookup, so the retype needs no DDL. `required` emits no NOT NULL.

## Pins (all on a real engine unless noted)

`src/preference-user-reference.integration.test.ts` (new, 13 tests):
- Declaration: an optional `sys_user` lookup, `cascade`, no width.
- Write door: `'*'` and `usr_nobody` → `code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'`, `mapDataError(...).status === 400`, a finding on `user_id` with code `reference_not_found`. An update moving a row to `'*'` is refused the same way. A real user and an empty User are accepted.
- Title:
  - `Bea Person · deal.won · inbox`;
  - the email where the name is blank;
  - `All users · deal.won · inbox`;
  - `All users · * · email` (topic default);
  - `null` for an id nobody holds.
- Cascade: deleting the user deletes their row; the global default stays, and no new global default appears.
- Conversion:
  - two organizations' `'*'` rows → empty, a real user's row untouched, `{status:'converted', converted:2}`;
  - the second run → `{status:'nothing-to-convert'}` and the rows are byte-identical;
  - no table → `absent`;
  - no engine → `no-engine`.
- Index on the SQL driver:
  - CONTROL: before the platform migrations, a second global default is accepted;
  - after the real `assembleMetadataProtocol` `kernel:ready` handlers run, it is refused `DUPLICATE_RECORD` / `409`;
  - other organizations, topics and channels, and a user's own row, are still accepted;
  - a `'*'` row that collides is kept, `reason: 'duplicate'`, and logged once at `error`.
  - driver-memory keys the listed columns and stays NULL-distinct, as it does for `sys_setting`. No test claims otherwise.
- Resolver end to end: an unconverted `'*'` mute stops nobody; after the conversion it mutes every user.

Other new pins:
- `messaging-service-plugin.test.ts`: the plugin arms the conversion. A `'*'` row becomes empty on `kernel:ready`, a second ready changes nothing, and one info line is logged.
- `metadata-protocol/src/migrations/notification-preference-identity-index.test.ts` (new, real SQLite):
  - before and after, per key, `''` and NULL in one bucket;
  - the declared name is reused, idempotent, the 18.0 COALESCE-organization form is rebuilt;
  - refuse-on-duplicates keeps the previous index and deletes nothing;
  - the `error` text and the listing query;
  - absent table, MySQL `unsupported`, and an unclassified failure.
- `metadata-protocol/src/plugin.notification-preference-index-armed.test.ts` (new): armed under `runPlatformMigrations`, and absent without it.
- `runtime-index-preflight.test.ts`: the preference probe reports `blocked` with the folded key, and the roster and statement-identity pins grow.

## Pins reversed (not deleted)

- `preference-resolver.test.ts`:
  - the fixture's default user is the empty reference instead of `'*'`;
  - "per-user row overrides the admin-global default" now uses an empty User;
  - new: every engine spelling of empty is the global default, and a stored `'*'` is not, with its control.
- `objects/notification-display-title.test.ts`: the preference case (raw-id title `usr_alice · billing.invoice · email`, `user_id` required) leaves the titleFormat-parity table. It is reversed in the new integration file: a person title, and an empty User accepted and titled `All users`. Delivery and receipt keep every assertion.
- `objects/notification-keyed-text-bounds.test.ts`: `user_id` was bounded to 255. It is now a lookup with no `maxLength`.
- `driver-sql/src/sql-driver-tenant-scoped-declared-unique.test.ts`: `'*'` → `'user_platform'` (above).
- `cli/src/commands/migrate/duplicates.contract.test.ts` and `.integration.test.ts`: the roster is four indexes.

- I ran the generator (`node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`) and updated the page's seven hand-written counts: 236 → 237 sites, 159 → 160 decidable, 134 → 135 elevated, and 50 → 51 const-named.
- The site is written so the census can place it fully: a same-file `const` typed `typeof PREFERENCE_OBJECT`, and an inline context carrying `isSystem` and the row's `tenantId`. No undecidable count moves.

## Acceptance notes

- The `All users` literal is English. Formula string literals are not translated; the field help is.
- `docs/adr/0030-notification-platform-convergence.md` (P2 row: "admin-global `*` defaults") records history on a governed surface and is left as is. `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/integration-system.json:1668` still says "'*' wildcards + admin-global default". That is still true of topic and channel, and the user half reads stale. Carrier: none.
- `sys_notification_delivery.display_title` has the same shape (`channel → recipient_id`). Per ruling item 5 it is the seat's separate card, not this PR.
- MySQL/MariaDB and driver-memory keep the declared, NULL-distinct index (`unsupported` is reported at `error` on MySQL), exactly as for `sys_setting`.

## The empty-state registry row (declared on #6017 `6334445279`)

`packages/spec/scripts/liveness/empty-state-registry.mts` carries one row:
- the file is the preference object, the property is `user_id`, and the semantics are `scope`;
- the rationale: an empty User selects which users a delivery toggle covers (the admin-wide default, ruling A `6304380498`) and grants no data access; a user's own row overrides it, mandatory topics bypass it, and `cascade` closes the set_null widening;
- the evidence is `preference-resolver.ts`'s `resolveRow`.

`check:empty-state` exits 0 with the row and 1 without it (`UNCLASSIFIED … notification-preference.object.ts:110 — user_id`), and the file was restored to `blob == HEAD`. Nothing else in `packages/spec` moves.

## The conversion's error text (`55663d72e`)

The boot conversion reports the engine error's message (a local `messageOf`), not `operatorFacingErrorText`. The `types` `test:repo` roster enumerates that helper's callers, which read the raw-SQL seam's composed fault, and this path issues no raw SQL: it goes through the data engine, whose SQL driver already redacts statements and bound values. Putting the helper call back reds exactly that roster test (1 failed of 11); restored.
